title: Finite-parts presentation of a pulled-back sheaf with proper support
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated quasi-finite morphism of finite presentation between Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-quasifinite, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Here Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $B$ be a commutative ring, and let $F,G$ be sheaves of $B$-modules on the small etale site $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $f^*$ for inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For a sheaf $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, let $f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}H\subset f_*H$ be the sheaf whose sections on $U\to S$ have support proper over $U$, as in [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition, def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

A finite-parts decomposition over an etale $U\to S$ of finite presentation consists of a finite pointed set $(I,0)$ and an open-and-closed disjoint decomposition $X\times_SU=\coprod_{i\in I}V_i$, where $v_i:V_i\to U$ is finite for $i\ne0$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. The piece $V_0$ need not be finite. There is a canonical map
$$\eta_\phi:(F|_U)^{\oplus(I\setminus\{0\})}\longrightarrow (f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f^*F)|_U$$
whose $i$-th component is the adjunction unit $F|_U\to v_{i*}v_i^*(F|_U)$ followed by inclusion as sections supported on the clopen finite piece $V_i$.

For a refinement $\phi'$ of $\phi$ specified by a pointed map $\sigma:I'\to I$ with $V_i=\coprod_{\sigma(j)=i}V'_j$ for every $i$, let $t_\sigma:F^{\oplus(I\setminus\{0\})}|_U\to F^{\oplus(I'\setminus\{0\})}|_U$ send a tuple $a$ to the tuple with $j$-th entry $a_{\sigma(j)}$ if $\sigma(j)\ne0$, and $0$ otherwise. Then $\eta_\phi=\eta_{\phi'}t_\sigma$.

These generators and relations give the following presentation: composing with all $\eta_\phi$ is a bijection between $B$-linear sheaf morphisms $f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f^*F\to G$ and families of $B$-linear maps $g_\phi:F^{\oplus(I\setminus\{0\})}|_U\to G|_U$ compatible with all etale restrictions and satisfying $g_\phi=g_{\phi'}t_\sigma$ for every refinement. Equivalently this is a colimit presentation in the etale-local sense [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; one can work on a small skeleton of the basis of finite-presentation etale objects. The generators commute with change of base under the proper-support comparison and with homomorphisms of coefficient rings.

For every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$ there is a pointed etale neighbourhood $U$ of finite presentation and such a decomposition for which $(V_0)_{\bar s}$ is empty and every $(V_i)_{\bar s}$ for $i\ne0$ has exactly one geometric point. The stalk of $\eta_\phi$ at this point is the isomorphism from one copy of $F_{\bar s}$ per point of $X_{\bar s}$ onto $(f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f^*F)_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

source.place: XVII 6.2.1, maps (6.2.1.1) and (6.2.1.2), Proposition 6.2.2 and its proof, pp. 420–422; the universal-property reformulation is the first two paragraphs of the proof of 6.2.3, p. 425. These are finite-parts presentation results, before the trace is constructed. No Stacks tag for this sheaf presentation was found.

proof.text: Fix a basis of finite-presentation etale objects. The Noetherian hypothesis implies that $S$ is locally Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes $S$ quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), every affine etale $U\to S$ is of finite presentation. The affine-shrink statement [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] gives such an affine pointed neighbourhood inside every given open neighbourhood of the marked point; objects of the small etale site are covered by these affine objects [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Thus all subsequent neighbourhoods may be replaced by objects of this basis. There is a set of isomorphism classes in this basis: refine further so that $U$ maps into one member $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of a fixed affine cover of $S$; its algebra is $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ for finite lists of polynomials, and these lists form a set. Morphisms between two such algebras form a set as well. Choosing representatives therefore gives a small basis; fibre products can be covered again by this basis. This is the size convention for the etale-local colimit, not an assumption that an arbitrary etale object is quasi-compact.

proof.text: Fix $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ and let $s$ be its image. Quasi-finiteness gives a finite list of all points of $X_s$ by [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres]; they are isolated by the definition [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-multiple-points] to this entire list. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is locally of finite type (indeed of finite type) and the listed fibre points are isolated. It gives an etale neighbourhood $(U,u)$ and finitely many finite opens $V_a\subset X_U$, each with a unique point $v_a$ over $u$ and purely inseparable residue extension $\kappa(v_a)/\kappa(u)$, the $v_a$ pairwise distinct and exhausting $(X_U)_u$. Choose a lift of $\bar s$ to $U$ over the chosen $u$ using the more precise clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], applied to the jointly surjective etale family consisting of $U\to S$ and the identity of $S$. Restrict to an affine neighbourhood of $u$ as in Step 1; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a) preserves finiteness of the opens after this restriction. If $X_s$ is empty use the trivial decomposition with only the remainder; no nonempty finite piece is introduced.

source.place: XVII Proposition 6.2.2, pp. 421–422, the decomposition at a geometric point; scheme-level finite neighbourhoods supplied by Stacks 02LM (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points-var)

proof.text: Make those opens into the required disjoint clopen decomposition. The base-changed map $X_U\to U$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change](1). Each $V_a\to U$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so its inclusion into $X_U$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]; its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. Thus $V_a$ is both open and closed in $X_U$. The intersection $V_a\cap V_b$ for $a\ne b$ is closed in the proper $U$-scheme $V_a$, hence proper over $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](b). Its fibre at $u$ is empty, since its unique possible points $v_a,v_b$ are distinct. Delete from $U$ the finitely many closed images of these intersections, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. The remaining open contains $u$, and the $V_a$ are now disjoint. Let $V_0$ be their clopen complement; it has empty fibre at $u$. For each $a\ne0$, the fibre $(V_a)_u\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ is radicial: it has a single point and purely inseparable residue extension. The equivalence of radicial and universally injective in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] implies that $(V_a)_{\bar s}$ has at most one point. It has a point because the purely inseparable residue field embeds in the algebraically closed $\Omega$, and the residue quotient followed by this embedding defines that point. Therefore each finite piece has exactly one geometric fibre point, and the remainder has none. Take an affine neighbourhood of $u$ again to retain finite presentation as in Step 1. This proves the asserted existence of special decompositions without assuming that $f$ is flat or etale.

proof.text: Construct the generators for an arbitrary decomposition $\phi$. Write $H=f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f^*F$, $u:U\to S$, $p:X_U\to X$ and $v:X_U\to U$. The map $p$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). Identify inverse image along $u$ and $p$ with restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction](1). The canonical proper-support comparison [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] then identifies $H|_U$ with $v_!^{\mathrm{supp}}p^{-1}f^*F$. Since $f\circ p=u\circ v$, the composition isomorphisms and their unit formulas [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units](1) identify $p^{-1}f^*F$ with $v^*(F|_U)$, preserving pulled-back sections. These are identifications of module sheaves: the actions and units have the stated underlying abelian-sheaf maps by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](2)–(3). By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), $v_i^*\dashv v_{i*}$ is the adjunction on $B$-module sheaves, with the underlying inverse-image unit. On any etale $T\to U$, pull a section $a\in F(T)$ back to $(V_i)_T$ by this unit, and extend it by zero on the other clopen pieces of $X_T$. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] glues these sections uniquely on this finite disjoint open cover. The resulting section has closed support contained in $(V_i)_T$, which is finite over $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Its closed support is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](2). It therefore belongs to $H(T)$, by the support-sheaf description [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition]. Add these component maps over $i\ne0$ to obtain $\eta_\phi$. Uniqueness of gluing and naturality of the unit make this a $B$-linear sheaf map, compatible with etale restriction and natural in $F$.

source.place: XVII 6.2.1, construction (6.2.1.1), p. 420; the proper-support interpretation uses Stacks 0F4X/0F51 (more-etale.tex, lemma-f-shriek-separated/lemma-proper-f-shriek)

proof.text: Check the relations and the elementary common refinement. On a refined piece $V'_j$, the section $\eta_\phi(a)$ is the pullback of $a_{\sigma(j)}$ if $\sigma(j)\ne0$, and zero otherwise. These are exactly the restrictions of $\eta_{\phi'}t_\sigma(a)$. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] gives equality on $X_T$ for every etale $T\to U$, hence equality in the support subsheaf. The same coordinate calculation gives $t_{\sigma\rho}=t_\rho t_\sigma$. Given two decompositions over $U$, take their intersections $V_i\cap W_j$ and label $(0,0)$ as the remainder. Every other intersection is closed in a finite piece of at least one of the decompositions; its inclusion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], and its map to $U$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. The two index projections are pointed refinement maps. This is an actual scheme-theoretic intersection of open subschemes, not a factorization of a general immersion through a subset.

source.place: XVII 6.2.1, square (6.2.1.2), pp. 420–421; common refinement in Proposition 6.2.2(i), with Stacks 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite) and 01WK (lemma-composition-finite)

proof.text:
Compute the generator on each geometric stalk. The special decomposition of Steps 2–3 identifies $C=X_{\bar s}$ with a finite disjoint union of finite $\Omega$-schemes, one point in each summand. The base-changed finite pieces are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a); iterating [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] makes $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ finite (the empty union is $\operatorname{Spec}0$ and is finite). Thus $C$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]; its underlying space is discrete, so it has dimension at most zero. Every closed support on $C$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](2). The restriction map of [lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk], followed by the germ isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-sections-stalks], gives
$$H_{\bar s}\cong H^0_c(C,(f^*F)|_C)=\Gamma(C,(f^*F)|_C)\cong\prod_{x\in|C|}(f^*F)_{\bar x}\cong\bigoplus_{x\in|C|}F_{\bar s}.$$
The last identifications use [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to the projection $C\to X$ and then to $f$, and finite product equals finite sum. The same lemma's unit formula identifies the map, not just its source and target: for ANY decomposition $\phi$, $\eta_{\phi,\bar s}$ sends a tuple $(a_i)_{i\ne0}$ to the tuple whose $x$-entry is $a_i$ when $x\in(V_i)_{\bar s}$ with $i\ne0$, and zero when $x\in(V_0)_{\bar s}$. The source stalk is the finite sum of $F_{\bar s}$ by [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits]. All maps are $B$-linear since they are restrictions and germs. For a special decomposition this matrix is the identity after indexing its nonzero labels by the fibre points, proving exactly the asserted stalk isomorphism.

It remains special: finite pieces stay finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), and its geometric fibre at the given lift is the same $\Omega$-scheme. Each of these intersections is finite over the base by Step 5, has empty geometric fibre at the marked point, hence empty ordinary fibre there (a nonzero finite algebra over a field has a point over an algebraic closure), and is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and misses the marked point. There are only finitely many intersections. After their deletion, $W_j\subseteq V_{i(j)}$ for $j

In particular, two presentations of a germ can be compared in a refinement whose generator is an isomorphism at that germ. No generator is asserted to be an isomorphism on an entire neighbourhood.

proof.text: Prove the universal property on actual sections. Suppose a restriction-compatible refinement-compatible family $g_\phi$ is given. For $h\in H(T)$ and each geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, take a special decomposition near its image in $S$ and pull it to a pointed neighbourhood of $\bar t$ in $T$; then take an affine neighbourhood as in Step 1. Its geometric fibre is unchanged, so it is still special. This procedure uses the original $f$ and does not apply a Noetherian-base assertion to an arbitrary non-quasi-compact etale $T$. By Step 6 the germ of $h$ has a unique tuple representative there. The neighbourhood category is cofiltered by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. Consequently, in the stalk colimit [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], finitely many representatives can be restricted to one common neighbourhood, and equality of two classes means equality after a further restriction: this is the equivalence relation defining a filtered colimit of sets. Represent the finitely many tuple coordinates this way; the equality with the germ of $h$ becomes an equality $h=\eta_\phi(a)$ after further restriction. These neighbourhoods, one over every point of $T$, form an etale cover. Assign to this local representative the section $g_\phi(a)$ of $G$. On an overlap compare two such representatives at any geometric point, and choose the special common refinement of Step 7. Their refined tuples have the same image under the injective stalk map $\eta_\theta$, hence are equal in the finite tuple stalk. The refinement relations for $g$ show that the two candidate values have equal germs. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sections-geometric-germ-ext] they agree as sections on the overlap. Glue them uniquely by [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. This defines $g_T(h)\in G(T)$ independently of all choices. Restricting the chosen cover proves restriction compatibility. To check addition and $B$-linearity, use common local refinements for the representatives of two sections; there both assertions are the corresponding assertions for $g_\theta$, so descend by uniqueness of gluing. For the generator identity, fix a tuple section $a$ for any $\phi$ and a geometric point. Represent $h=\eta_\phi(a)$ locally by a tuple $b$ for a special decomposition $\psi$ as above. Take a special common refinement $\theta$ with maps $\sigma:I_\theta\to I_\phi$ and $\rho:I_\theta\to I_\psi$. Step 5 gives $\eta_\theta(t_\sigma a)=h=\eta_\theta(t_\rho b)$. Injectivity of $\eta_\theta$ at the chosen stalk gives $(t_\sigma a)_{\bar t}=(t_\rho b)_{\bar t}$, so the family relations give $(g_\phi(a))_{\bar t}=(g_\theta(t_\sigma a))_{\bar t}=(g_\theta(t_\rho b))_{\bar t}=(g_\psi(b))_{\bar t}=(g(h))_{\bar t}$. Germ extensionality now proves $g\eta_\phi=g_\phi$. The morphism is unique because every section of $H$ locally has a generator representative. Conversely a sheaf map gives such a family by Step 5 and restriction. These constructions are inverse. This is the asserted etale-local colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with the size convention of Step 1.

proof.text: Check base change on the maps just constructed. For a Cartesian square with base map $b:S'\to S$ and projection $a:X'\to X$, use the canonical comparison $b^{-1}H\cong f'_!{}^{\mathrm{supp}}a^{-1}f^*F$ of [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition]. An etale object $U\to S$ pulls back to an etale object $U'=U\times_SS'\to S'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1), and it is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Clopen pieces pull back to clopen pieces (inverse images of both the open and its complementary open), and finite pieces remain finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Inverse image preserves finite sums by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), and its module units are the underlying abelian-sheaf units by the same clause. Its composition identifications respect pulled-back unit sections by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units](1); those identifications also identify $a^{-1}f^*F$ with $f'^*b^{-1}F$. The support comparison is the restriction of the ordinary pullback comparison on direct images, so it sends a unit section on $V_i$ extended by zero to the pulled-back unit section on $V_i\times_SS'$ extended by zero. More explicitly, at a geometric point of $S'$, both composites send $(a_i)$ to the tuple with entry $a_i$ on the base-changed finite piece labelled $i$, and zero on its remainder, by Step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Equality on these germs implies equality of maps on sections by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sections-geometric-germ-ext]. This proves base-change compatibility of every generator and relation. This verification applies to any base map $b$: Step 4 constructs the pulled-back generator using its given finite clopen pieces, and its stalk calculation uses $X'_{\bar s'}\cong X_{b\bar s'}$, so the finite-fibre calculation of Step 6 applies directly. Neither constructing a new basis on $S'$ nor assuming $S'$ Noetherian is required; the support comparison has no flatness restriction on $b$.

proof.text:
Check coefficient homomorphisms, with ordinary sheaf scalar extension. Restriction of scalars changes no underlying section, support, refinement matrix or unit-section formula. For $B\to B'$ put $F'=B'\otimes_BF$, defined by sectionwise scalar extension followed by sheafification [def-pod-ring-scalar-extension]. The ordinary module adjunction on each section, together with the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], gives the sheaf scalar-extension/restriction adjunction: a map out of $B'\otimes_BM$ is precisely a compatible family of balanced maps $B'\times M(T)\to N(T)$, equivalently a $B$-linear sheaf map $M\to\operatorname{Res}N$. Naturality in $F$ from Step 4 applied to $F\to\operatorname{Res}F'$ therefore defines a canonical map
$$c:B'\otimes_B(f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f^*F)\longrightarrow f_!^{\mathrm{supp}}f^*(B'\otimes_BF).$$
By [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar](2) and the identifications in Step 6, its stalk is the canonical map
$$B'\otimes_B\bigoplus_xF_{\bar s}\longrightarrow\bigoplus_x(B'\otimes_BF_{\bar s}),\qquad b'\otimes(a_x)_x\longmapsto(b'\otimes a_x)_x.$$
It is an isomorphism, with inverse the sum of the tensor maps of the summand inclusions; the empty sum case is zero. Thus $c$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to underlying abelian sheaves. Under $c$ the scalar extension of each generator is the generator for $F'$: on tensor elements the coordinate formula of Step 6 is unchanged, and [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sections-geometric-germ-ext] makes the equality a sheaf equality. In particular the same diagonal and zero matrices give all refinement relations over $B'$. No exactness or flatness of $B'\otimes_B-$ is used. This completes all coefficient and base-change clauses.

split_report.summary: Proved the SGA finite-parts presentation in ten steps using only existing DAG statements. Built disjoint finite opens via 02LM and proper closed images, calculated the exact generator on stalks, and descended compatible maps by actual local representatives, good common refinements, and sheaf gluing. Included small-basis, arbitrary base-change and ordinary coefficient-extension checks. No new nodes or mathematical statement correction; added the missing colimit-definition citation. Second reading made the localization identifications and generator identity explicit, and checked generator base change for arbitrary base schemes.
split_report.blueprint: Seed refinement of sk-thm-purity-transport Step 1, finite trace construction: SGA 4 XVII 6.2.1 and Proposition 6.2.2 supply the generators and refinement relations used to construct the quasi-finite trace in XVII 6.2.3, proof p. 425. This seed chain has no imported blueprint ancestor. Steps 1–3 and 6 realize the local finite-parts reduction; Steps 4–5 construct (6.2.1.1–2); Steps 7–8 prove the presentation of 6.2.2 used in the seed trace construction; Steps 9–10 give its functorialities.
